## Dangers

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- BVDOutbreakSize. 658 merged pull requests since 19 May
- Agents push towards complex, nested models and code
- Not written the way a person would write it. Hard to follow and review
- Wrong observation models and forecast bugs. We caught them
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}

## Google's tree search topped the CDC forecast hubs

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- An LLM-guided tree search that writes forecasting code. First in the
  CDC FluSight hub, 2025/26
- Most candidates adapt models already in the hubs
- Aygün et al. claimed a gain in retrospect. It came from data revisions
  leaking into the evaluation
- 207,500 candidate models. My guess is few groups have that compute
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](figures/agents-martinson2026-fig2.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Inputs of a problem statement, data, libraries and evaluation
requirements feed a tree of candidate models, each node coloured by its
score, with the best leaf circled and the forecasting code it produced,
an SIR model fitted with scipy, shown as the output."}

::: {.attribution}
Figure 2 of Martinson et al. 2026,
